title: Developing a Theologically Rooted Christian Vision
description:
This course is designed as an introduction for school leaders to:

  • Explore what we mean by vision in a Church school context

  • Reflect upon the theological underpinning of our school vision and its connection to educational practice

  • Consider the ways in which we communicate our strategic vision and the impact it has

 

This could be used by headteachers, SLT and governors as they review and develop a theologically rooted Christian vision for their school.

title: EDIJ 1: A Christian Vision for Racial Inclusion
description: This session explores the theological underpinning for racial inclusion in Church schools and how your school’s Christian vision drives this work.

title: EDIJ 2: Becoming an Antiracist School
description: In this session Allana Gay explores how to move a school community beyond being not racist/‘colour-blind’ to anti-racist.

title: EDIJ 3: Racial Justice – Policies & Parents
description: Through this session, Allana Gay will support you with writing and evaluating school policies to ensure there is not disproportional impact on particular communities. The session also explores building a working understanding with parents around race in education so that they can support the work you do in school.

title: EDIJ 4: Racial Justice – An Antiracist Curriculum
description: This session supports you to evaluate impactful representation and ‘normalised’ (or ‘usualised’) presence of diverse people, histories and cultures across your curriculum.

title: Introducing the Religion & Worldviews Approach and Disciplinary Knowledge in RE
description: In this session, Gillian Georgiou explains the three types of knowledge in RE (substantive, disciplinary & personal), with a focus on disciplinary knowledge. You will be introduced to the ‘Religion & Worldviews approach’ and how it differs from the ‘World Religions approach’ that we have used in the past. With theoretical underpinning alongside practical ideas, this CPD is designed to fit into a staff meeting or RE department meeting to support you to introduce these ideas to teachers of RE in your school.

title: Justice & Responsibility CPD for Staff Meetings
description: A session those who want to think through what it might mean to create, and live out, a culture of justice and responsibility in their school. An opportunity to explore this area of school life with questions to reflect upon, as well as some worked examples and ideas to try out. This session could be used as staff training.

title: Justice & Responsibility Introduction for School Leaders
description: A short introduction to the idea of creating a culture of justice and responsibility for leaders. This could be used at an SLT or governor meeting.

title: Understanding Christianity Refresher (Introduction)
description: This session is aimed at teachers new to using the Understanding Christianity resources or those who would like a refresher. It aims to support you to gain a working knowledge of the Understanding Christianity resource including, the key theological concepts covered in the resource, the ‘Big Story of the Bible’ and how to use the ‘big frieze’. It also explores how to plan using the Understanding Christianity resource, outlining what’s included and how to use it, the pedagogy of the resource and how to access everything online.

title: Spiritual Styles and Spiritual Flourishing through Collective Worship
description: In this session, Dr Ryan Parker, explores how we might arrive at a shared understanding of spirituality in school to support spiritual flourishing. By reflecting on ‘spiritual styles’ you will consider how to plan for and support spiritual development through collective worship so that pupils and adults can flourish spiritually in your school.

title: Introduction to Collective Worship
description:
This course aims to help those new to leading collective worship to:

  • Know the legal requirements around collective worship and what collective worship is and is not.

  • Explore the role and importance of collective worship in a church school as an expression of your theologically rooted Christian vision.

  • Reflect upon how collective worship contributes to the spiritual flourishing of pupils and adults in your school.

  • Consider some key principles to enable you plan for and lead collective worship that is inclusive, invitational and inspiring.
